question.text: Which of the following best describes the role of banks in mutual fund distribution?

answer.text: Banks can only distribute mutual funds managed by their own group AMCs
Banks act as RTAs for mutual fund schemes they distribute
Banks act as corporate distributors using their branch network to sell mutual fund schemes of various AMCs
Banks guarantee the returns of mutual fund schemes they distribute to their customers

explanation.text: The Logic: Banks and bank branches are a prominent non-individual/institutional distribution channel for mutual funds (workbook pp. 115-116). An AMC may appoint a bank as a distributor (workbook p. 120), and bank employees engaged in MF sales require AMFI registration, empanelment, and an Employee Unique Identification Number (workbook pp. 121-122). Mutual fund investments are not guaranteed or assured-return products (workbook p. 309). The Trap: Option A is wrong because the workbook describes banks as distributors of multiple AMCs' schemes, not just group AMCs. Option B is wrong because RTAs are separate entities (CAMS, KFintech). Option D is the most dangerous distractor: banks do not guarantee mutual fund returns. Note: Bank distribution still relies on the standard AMFI registration, empanelment, and EUIN framework that applies to other non-individual distributors.
